note: River access on the Lamine River off Route M near I-70, with a boat ramp. The camp sites are gravel pull-ins off a gravel lane that runs along the river from the ramp lot to a turnaround, under scattered trees with the river through the bank trees. --Claude

Pin on the camp lane, fine. Riverview kept (spurs ~25-30 m from the water across open lawn, behind a bank tree line). PHONE MISMATCH: page (573) 445-3882, stored 573-815-7900.
flags: INCLUSION/FIT: area page 'Harriman Hill Access is a 30 acre area located on the Lamine River. There is a boat ramp, 6 individual camp sites and a privy located on the area'; 'Things to Do When You Visit: Camping: Individual Campsites'; Rule 140 standard text, no permit rule. Map (05/16) legend 'Primitive Camping Area'; one symbol on the gravel road SE of the ramp lot (= GIS 310, 138 m from lot 1482). Imagery: a gravel lane continues ~200 m SE from the ramp lot along the river with five or six gravel pull-in spurs (~10-15 m) toward the river and a gravel turnaround at the end - a small designated camp, a 23-ft rig fits. No horse camp, ford or rig wording; the road in is gravel off paved Route M.

WATERFRONT (riverview, kept): the spur ends are ~25-30 m from the Lamine River across mown grass with scattered trees, then a tree line along the (cut) bank; in the leaf-on frame the bank canopy is continuous, in the leaf-off frame the water shows plainly through open trunks. A continuous bank tree line is a buffer, so not riverfront; the filtered view from the spurs holds, so riverview stays.
